name: England under Edward I
blurb: Watermills and windmills everywhere, a real legal system, chartered towns, universities, the horse collar, the crank, the mechanical clock arriving, and about to be hit by the worst demographic catastrophe in European history.

institutions.corporation: borough and guild corporations, genuinely perpetual
institutions.note: A PERPETUAL CORPORATION EXISTS HERE and it is the single most important institutional advantage over Rome: an enterprise can outlive its founder without a testamentary trick.

values._note: w_religious_rigidity 0.8 and w_magic_fear 0.7: this is the environment that produced heresy trials and, later, witch trials. Far more dangerous for a natural philosopher than Trajanic Rome, which had no doctrine to offend. Guilds resist labour-saving machinery violently and have legal standing to do it.
values._note_eminence: A king who can attaint you, but also chartered towns, guilds and a church with its own courts, so power is more divided than in Rome.

notes: You arrive 48 years before the Black Death kills something like 45% of the population.
The perpetual corporation is worth more to a multi-generation programme than any machine in the tree.
Guilds will litigate against your fulling mill. They did, repeatedly, and sometimes won.
_note_cost_multipliers: Wool is the English economy and the whole textile chain is cheaper here than anywhere. Chartered towns, guilds and a money economy make commerce easier than in Rome. Against that: a much smaller population and a king who can attaint you.
